name: server_action_sort
summary: Lets an admin set up a Sort action so users can reorder the lines of any list, such as sale order lines, by chosen criteria. The action appears in the Action menu of that model's list view after selecting records. It is configured under Settings, Technical, Actions, Server Actions.

name: attachment_delete_restrict
summary: Stops users from deleting attachments (files attached to records) unless they are allowed to. Permissions can be set globally or per model, for example limiting deletion to the record owner, admins, or specific groups or users. It is configured in General Settings under Permissions and in each model's settings.

name: attachment_queue
summary: A technical base module that wraps file attachments in a queue so they can be processed in the background. Each queued file has a type, state, done date and failure message, and admins can reschedule failed files from Settings, Technical, Database Structure, Attachments Queue. It is mainly used by other modules such as attachment_synchronize.

name: attachment_queue_email
summary: Automatically turns email attachments into queued files based on conditions such as sender, recipient, subject or file extension. Each matching attachment is added to the attachment queue for later processing. The conditions are set on the Incoming Mail Server (Fetchmail) configuration.

name: attachment_synchronize
summary: Imports files from external storage servers (such as SFTP or S3) into Odoo and exports files from Odoo back out. Import and export are scheduled as tasks that define where to look, which files match, and what happens to the source files afterwards. Tasks are found under Settings, Technical.

name: attachment_unindex_content
summary: Turns off the storing of extracted text from attachments, which saves database space and processing time. It also clears the stored text from existing attachments when installed. Users are not affected in day-to-day use, but full text search inside attached files will no longer work.

name: auditlog
summary: Keeps a record of who created, viewed, changed, deleted or exported data in chosen models, including old and new field values. Admins define which models and operations to log under Settings, Technical, Audit, Rules, and review the results under Audit, Logs. Logs older than 6 months can be cleared by an optional scheduled action.

name: auto_backup
summary: Creates automatic backups of the database on a schedule, deletes old backups after a set number of days, and can send copies to an external server over SFTP. Backup configurations are set under Settings, Database Structure, Automated Backup. It is an admin tool with no effect on daily users.

name: autovacuum_message_attachment
summary: Automatically deletes old chatter messages, emails and attachments based on rules that set the model, message type and number of days to keep. This keeps the database from growing too large over time. Rules are configured under Settings, Technical, Email, Message and Attachment Vacuum Rules.

name: base_conditional_image
summary: Lets admins define images that change depending on record details, such as a different logo per company or a default image for records that match a condition. The same image is stored once and reused, so changing it updates every matching record. Images are set under Settings, Technical, Images.

name: base_cron_exclusion
summary: Lets admins mark scheduled actions that must not run at the same time, so two heavy jobs never overlap. The setting is on the scheduled action form under a Mutually Exclusive Scheduled Actions tab. It is a technical setting found under Settings, Technical, Automation, Scheduled Actions.

name: base_exception
summary: A base framework for defining configurable exception rules, such as blocking a sale order when a condition is not met. It provides the exception popup and resolution wizard that other modules use. It is not useful alone; it shows up in the apps that build on it, like sales or purchase exceptions.

name: base_fontawesome
summary: Adds the Font Awesome 6.5.1 icon library to Odoo so icons can be used in views, websites and reports. Solid, regular and brand icon styles are supported. It is a technical resource with no new screens for users.

name: base_fontawesome_web_editor
summary: Makes Font Awesome 6.7.2 and newer icons display correctly in the website and web editor. It installs automatically once the web editor and base Font Awesome modules are present. Users see the icons in the editor without any extra setup.

name: base_force_record_noupdate
summary: Lets admins mark a model so its data is protected from being overwritten when modules are upgraded. The option is a checkbox on the model form under Settings, Technical, Models, labelled Force No-Update. It is a technical safeguard for developers and administrators.

name: base_m2m_custom_field
summary: A technical field type that lets developers create many-to-many relationships with direct access to the link table. This makes it possible to edit those links in their own list view. It has no screens of its own and is used by developers building custom features.

name: base_model_restrict_update
summary: Lets admins make a model read-only for most users, with exemptions for chosen groups, or revoke editing rights for a specific user. Configured on the model form and the user form under Settings, Technical. It is a security tool for locking down data.

name: base_multi_image
summary: Lets any record, such as a product or partner, hold a gallery of several images instead of one. Images can be managed from Settings, Technical, Multi Images. It is a base module that other apps, such as product image galleries, build on.

name: base_name_search_improved
summary: Makes searching in relation fields much more forgiving, so typing words in a different order or missing a middle name still finds the right record. If few results are found, it also searches other fields such as city or phone, which admins can configure per model. This affects dropdown lookups like choosing a customer on a sales order, not the top search bar.

name: base_partition
summary: A technical helper that splits a set of records into groups by a field value, such as separating paid and unpaid invoices in code. It adds a partition method to every model. Users see no change; it is for developers.

name: base_remote
summary: Keeps a list of the network addresses that have connected to Odoo, storing each hostname, its last IP address and whether it is inside the company network. The list is viewable under Settings, Remotes. It is a technical helper for other modules and for security checks.

name: base_search_fuzzy
summary: Adds fuzzy text matching to the database so searches can find near-spelling matches, such as John Smit for John Smith. Admins can add trigram indexes on text fields under Settings, Database Structure, Trigram Index. It is a technical base module used by developers and does not change existing searches.

name: base_sequence_option
summary: Lets admins set up alternate numbering for documents, so for example customer invoices for one customer or region use a different number sequence than the default. Rules are matched on document values and configured under Settings, Technical, Sequences, Manage Sequence Options. It is a base module that document-specific add-ons build on.

name: base_sparse_field_list_support
summary: A technical helper that lets list values be stored in a serialized field and read back correctly. It is for developers and has no screens for users.

name: base_technical_user
summary: Lets a company be linked to an inactive technical user that background and batch processes run under. A helper method lets developers run code as that user, or as the superuser if none is set. The setting appears in a tab on the company form under Settings, Companies.

name: base_temporary_action
summary: A technical helper that lets developers mark actions as temporary so they are removed automatically after about an hour. It does nothing visible on its own. Used by developers when a short-lived window or action is needed.

name: base_time_parameter
summary: Lets admins store settings whose value changes over time, such as a tax rate or a fee that starts on a given date. Each parameter has dated versions, and the correct value for a date is picked automatically. It is found under Settings, Technical, Time Parameters.

name: base_time_window
summary: A technical base for records that are only valid during certain time windows, such as opening hours or delivery slots on specific weekdays. It checks that windows do not overlap for the same parent record. Developers use it in other modules; users do not see it on its own.

name: base_url
summary: A technical base that gives records clean, stable web addresses based on a key instead of a database ID, and redirects old addresses when a key changes. It was built for online shops that need unique links per record. Users see nothing by default; developers use it in other modules.

name: base_view_inheritance_extension
summary: A technical add-on that extends how view customizations are written, adding extra operators for editing dictionaries, text and domains inside views. It is for developers who customize screens, and nothing changes for end users.

name: bus_alt_connection
summary: A technical add-on for installations that use PgBouncer as a database connection pooler. It lets the Odoo bus (live notifications) connect directly to the database with its own settings. Only administrators running this kind of server setup need it.

name: database_autovacuum_tuning
summary: Shows administrators recommended PostgreSQL autovacuum thresholds for their database, with guidance on sizing them. Values can be overridden with system parameters, and the page is under Settings, Technical, Database Structure, Database Autovacuum Tuning. It is mainly useful for PostgreSQL 17 and older.

name: database_cleanup
summary: A risky administrator tool that finds leftover models, fields, tables, menus and data from uninstalled modules and lets the admin purge them. It is found under Settings, Technical, Database Cleanup and only Access Rights administrators can see it. Misuse can damage data, so it should only be used by experienced developers.

name: database_size
summary: Takes a daily snapshot of how much disk space the database and attachments use, and shows how the size of each model has changed over time. Reports are under Settings, Technical, Database, with an option to keep only a set number of older measurements. It helps admins watch growth and plan storage.

name: dbfilter_from_header
summary: Lets a web server choose which database to open by sending the database filter in an HTTP header. This is for hosting setups where database names cannot be matched to host names. It is an infrastructure setting with no effect on users.

name: excel_import_export
summary: A developer toolkit for building Excel exports, imports and reports from Excel templates, where layout and formulas are designed in Excel and filled with Odoo data. Templates are managed under Settings, Technical, Excel Templates, and wizards let users export or import using them. Developers use it to add spreadsheet reports to their apps.

name: fetchmail_attach_from_folder
summary: Files emails from chosen mail server folders onto matching records, such as attaching an email to a contact found by its email address. Matching can use the exact address, the domain or the standard Odoo rule. Folders and matching rules are set on the Incoming Mail Server (Fetchmail) form.

name: fetchmail_notify_error_to_sender
summary: Sends an automatic reply to the sender when Odoo cannot process an incoming email, so mistakes such as writing to a wrong address are not silently lost. The reply uses an editable email template set on the Incoming Mail Server. Admins configure it on the mail server form.

name: field_vector
summary: A technical add-on that adds a new Vector field type for storing lists of numbers, such as the data used by AI or similarity search. It is for developers building features on top of it. Users do not interact with it directly.

name: html_text
summary: A technical utility that extracts plain text from rich text (HTML) fields, with an option to shorten it by words or characters and add an ellipsis. It is used by developers to build short previews. Users see no screens from it.

name: iap_alternative_provider
summary: A technical base for connecting Odoo's IAP service, used for paid services such as SMS, to an alternative provider. It adds a provider choice on the IAP account. It is used by developers of connector modules.

name: jsonifier
summary: A developer tool that converts records into JSON data using a simple description of which fields to include, with options for nested records and custom field names. It can also use saved export profiles to define the output. Developers use it to build APIs and integrations.

name: mail_cleanup
summary: Marks old incoming emails as read and moves them to a folder, and deletes old messages from the mail server before fetching new ones. Retention periods are set per incoming mail server. It keeps the shared mailbox tidy and stops unrouted junk mail from piling up.

name: mail_template_attachment_per_lang
summary: Automatically adds attachments to email templates based on the recipient's language, such as sending the right language version of terms and conditions. The language method and attachments are set on the email template under Settings, Technical, Email, Templates. Users see the correct files added when they pick that template in the email composer.

name: module_analysis
summary: Shows how much of the installed code comes from Odoo core, OCA, or custom in-house modules, with counts of Python, XML, JavaScript and style lines. Rules decide each module's type and are maintained under Apps, Module Analysis. It helps companies estimate upgrade effort and technical debt.

name: module_auto_update
summary: Upgrades only the installed modules whose code has changed since the last successful upgrade, instead of upgrading everything. It works by comparing saved checksums of each module's files. It is an administrator tool for maintenance and deployments.

name: module_change_auto_install
summary: Lets administrators change which modules install automatically through the server configuration file, adding or removing modules from the automatic install list. It is a server-level setting set in the Odoo configuration file, not in the app. End users see no difference except which modules are present.

name: odoo_test_xmlrunner
summary: A developer add-on that runs Odoo's automated tests and produces XML test reports that continuous integration systems can read. It only changes how tests are run and reported. End users are not affected.

name: onchange_helper
summary: A developer helper that runs the automatic field updates that normally happen on screen, such as filling a customer's address after choosing them, when values are set from code or import. It is a technical module with no screens of its own. Developers call it from their Python code.

name: rpc_helper
summary: Lets developers and administrators block selected external API calls, such as create or write, on a given model. Blocking can be set in code or in the model's RPC config tab in debug mode. It is a security tool to stop outside systems from changing sensitive data.

name: scheduler_error_mailer
summary: Emails a chosen template to a contact whenever a scheduled action fails with an error. This lets someone know quickly when an automatic job breaks. The template is picked on each scheduled action under Settings, Technical, Automation, Scheduled Actions.

name: sentry
summary: Sends Odoo server errors and warnings to a Sentry error-tracking service so developers are alerted to problems. It is set up through the Odoo configuration file with a Sentry key. End users see no change.

name: sentry_client
summary: Sends JavaScript errors from the browser part of Odoo to Sentry, with optional performance tracking and session replay that are off by default. Settings are under Settings, General Settings, Sentry Browser, and individual users can opt out of session replay in their preferences. The Sentry library is included so no outside connection is needed to load it.

name: sequence_python
summary: Lets a sequence number be calculated from a Python formula, for example to add separators, use UUIDs, or hide the true count of orders from customers. The formula is entered on the Python tab of a sequence record under Settings, Technical, Sequences. Administrators use it to build custom numbering schemes.

name: session_db
summary: Stores user login sessions in a database instead of on the server's disk, which makes it easier to run several Odoo servers behind a load balancer. It is set up through the server configuration and an environment variable. Users notice no difference, but it is useful for scaled hosting.

name: tracking_manager
summary: Lets admins track changes to all fields of a model in the chatter, including one2many and many2many lines, so line-level edits such as quantity changes on sale order lines are logged. Tracking is enabled per model under Settings, Technical, Models, Custom Tracking. Fields can be picked by hand or by a domain.

name: tracking_manager_domain
summary: Adds an optional condition to field tracking, so a change is only logged in the chatter when a chosen domain is met. It extends Tracking Manager and is configured on each tracked field. It keeps the chatter from filling up with changes that do not matter.

name: upgrade_analysis
summary: A migration tool that compares the data model and modules of two Odoo versions or instances to produce analysis files used when upgrading. It is intended for developers running upgrades and should not be kept on a live production database. End users have no reason to use it.

name: announcement
summary: Shows pop-up announcements to chosen internal users when they log in, which they must mark as read, and keeps a log of who has read each one. Announcements can be rich text and targeted to specific users or groups, and are managed under Discuss, Announcements by users in the Announcements Managers group. Unread items can also be reopened from the top bar.

name: barcode_action
summary: Lets a barcode scan launch an action, such as scanning a partner's external reference to open that partner's record. Each action is configured with the model, the method to run and an optional record. It builds on the barcode module and is used by developers to add scan shortcuts.

name: base_cancel_confirm
summary: A base feature that adds a confirmation popup asking for a reason when a document's cancel button is clicked, and shows that reason on the form. It does nothing on its own and is switched on for specific apps such as sales or purchases through system parameters. Developers use it to add the same behavior to other documents.

name: base_custom_filter
summary: Lets admins add their own search filters, group-by options and search fields to list views, shown in the standard filter and group-by menus. They are created under Settings, Custom Filters, and can be limited to chosen user groups. It helps teams find records faster on each app's screen.

name: base_export_manager
summary: Lets admins manage the export templates that users save, and adds an export access right per model so some groups can be blocked from exporting data. Export templates are kept under Settings, Technical, User Interface, Export Templates. It is useful for controlling data leaving the system.

name: base_import_security_group
summary: Makes importing CSV and Excel files a permission that admins can grant per user, using an Import CSV/Excel Files checkbox on the user form. Users without it no longer see the Import records button in list and kanban views, and batch imports are blocked on the server too. It is used to keep data loading restricted.

name: base_menu_visibility_restriction
summary: Hides chosen menu items from users who belong to particular groups, so each user only sees the menus meant for them. Excluded groups are set on each menu item in debug mode, under Settings, Technical, User Interface, Menu Items. It is a simple way to tidy up menus per role.

name: base_optional_quick_create
summary: Stops the Create quick option from appearing in dropdowns for chosen models, so users must open the full form to add a new record. It is switched on per model under Settings, Technical, Models, Avoid Quick Create. It helps keep records like contacts from being created with incomplete details.

name: base_revision
summary: A base feature for keeping earlier versions of a document when it is revised, such as a sale order that is copied as a new revision with an incremented number. Old revisions are archived and listed on the document. It does nothing alone; the sale order revision module is the example that uses it.

name: base_search_custom_field_filter
summary: Lets admins define extra search filters on fields of a document or related documents, which then appear in the search bar for all users. Filters are created under Settings, Technical, User Interface, Custom Field Filters. A demo filter is included to show how it works.

name: base_substate
summary: A base feature for adding sub-statuses within a main status, such as In Negotiation, Won or Lost under a quotation, and optionally sending an email when one is reached. It does nothing alone; app modules like purchase substate use it. Users see the sub-status on the document.

name: base_technical_features
summary: Gives users a Technical features preference that unlocks technical menus and views without turning on debug mode. It is switched on by default for all users at install time. It is used by administrators and developers who need technical screens day to day.

name: base_tier_validation
summary: A base feature for requiring one or more people to approve a document before it can be used, in ordered tiers such as a manager and then a director. Admins define tiers under Settings, Technical, Tier Validations, Tier Definition, and approvals are shown on the document. It does nothing alone; apps like purchase tier validation use it.

name: base_tier_validation_confirm_auth
summary: Requires an approver to re-enter their login password before approving or rejecting a tier review. It is turned on per tier definition with a Require Authentication checkbox. It adds an extra safeguard to approvals.

name: base_tier_validation_correction
summary: Lets a user with the Tier Review Correction role change who the reviewer is on a pending approval, for example when the original approver is away. Corrections are made under Settings, Technical, Tier Validation, Tier Review Correction. It keeps approvals moving without cancelling the document.

name: base_tier_validation_formula
summary: Lets admins write Python code to decide when a tier applies and who the reviewers are, rather than only using a domain filter. The formula is chosen on each tier definition under Settings, Technical, Tier Validations. It gives approval rules more flexibility.

name: base_tier_validation_forward
summary: Lets an approver forward a pending approval to another person when they do not want to decide themselves, with the new reviewer added to the approval chain. The option is enabled per tier definition with Allow Forward. Users see a Forward button next to Approve and Reject.

name: base_tier_validation_server_action
summary: Lets a tier definition run a server action automatically when the tier is approved or rejected, such as sending a notification or updating a field. Tiers can also be validated automatically by a scheduled job when a condition is met. Set up on each tier definition under Settings, Technical, Tier Validations.

name: base_user_locale
summary: Lets each company, and each user, override regional display settings such as date format, time format, first day of the week, and decimal and thousands separators. Company settings are under Settings, General Settings, Locale, and user settings are in each user's preferences. It changes how numbers and dates look for the people it is set for.

name: base_warn_option
summary: A base feature that gives warning and blocking messages standard options for who can see them and how they are used, so warnings stay consistent across apps. Warning options are kept under the settings for warnings. It is a technical base that other modules use for their pop-up messages.

name: chained_swapper
summary: Lets a field value, such as the delivery address on a confirmed sales order, be changed and automatically passed on to linked records like its delivery orders, with rules that can block the change when a linked record is already validated. Admins define the swaps under Settings, Field Swaps, and users run them from the Action menu of a list. It should be used carefully because a wrong setup can leave data inconsistent.

name: date_range
summary: Lets admins define named date periods such as fiscal years, quarters or months, and use them to filter list views. A wizard can generate recurring periods automatically. Date ranges and types are under Settings, Technical, Date Ranges, and any model can add a period search field to its search bar.

name: date_range_account
summary: Adds the Date Range menu to the Invoicing app so accounting managers can reach it directly. It is a small link module between Date Range and Accounting. Accountants use it to set up their fiscal periods from the Invoicing configuration menu.

name: default_multi_user
summary: Lets an admin share a user-defined default value, such as a default field setting for a form, with chosen users or groups. The sharing is set on the default record under Settings, Technical, Actions, User-defined Defaults. It saves each person from setting the same default themselves.

name: developer_menu
summary: Adds a Developer menu next to the Technical menu that gathers the most-used technical screens in one place, so developers save time finding them. It is visible to users in the Administration or ERP manager group. It changes navigation only and adds no data.

name: document_quick_access
summary: Lets users scan a barcode or QR code, or type one, to jump straight to a record such as a sale order or a product. Printed reports can carry a QR code for fast lookup, and a search launcher opens with a shortcut in the top bar. Rules that link each barcode format to a model are set under Settings, Technical, Document Quick Access.

name: document_quick_access_folder_auto_classification
summary: Scans files dropped into a storage folder, such as scanned documents, and attaches each one to the record its QR code points to. Files that match no code are kept as unprocessed documents for someone to assign by hand. It is a background job that depends on the document quick access rules and an external storage setup.

name: filter_multi_user
summary: Lets admins share a saved custom filter with chosen users or groups, so the same filter appears in their Favorites list. Only the owner can edit the filter. Sharing is set on the filter record under Settings, Technical, User Interface, User-defined Filters.

name: mail_message_destiny_link_template
summary: Provides a developer email template that writes a chatter note on the source record linking to the records it created, such as a purchase order noting the invoice it produced. It is a building block for developers and has no screens by itself. Users see the note only where a developer uses it.

name: multi_step_wizard
summary: A technical base for building wizards that move through several steps, with the option to go back to the previous step. It does nothing on its own. Developers use it to build guided multi-page dialogs in other modules.

name: sequence_check_digit
summary: Adds a check digit to the end of document numbers so typos can be caught visually or by integrations. Several standard check methods can be chosen on each sequence under Settings, Technical, Sequences. It is useful where numbers are read or typed by hand, such as labels or manual references.

name: sequence_reset_period
summary: Lets document numbers restart on a chosen schedule, such as monthly, weekly or daily, instead of only yearly. The reset period is set on each sequence under Settings, Technical, Sequences. It is useful when numbering needs to restart more often than once a year.

name: server_action_mass_edit
summary: Lets users change the same field on many selected records at once from the Action menu of a list, with a choice to set or remove the value. Admins define which fields can be mass edited through a server action of the new Mass Edit type under Settings, Technical, Server Actions. It saves time when many records need the same change.

name: server_action_mass_edit_onchange
summary: Extends Mass Edit so that automatic field updates, the same ones that fire when a user types on a form, run after a bulk change. This keeps related fields consistent when many records are changed together. It is configured on the mass edit server action.

name: template_content_swapper
summary: Lets admins replace wording in printed reports, emails and web pages without writing custom code, for example changing Salesperson to Sales Representative on quotations. Each replacement is a mapping record set up under Settings, Technical, User Interface, Template Content Mappings. Changes can be set per language.

name: stock_request
summary: Lets employees request stock they regularly need to be moved to their chosen location, such as supplies for a team. Each request is evaluated by the location's replenishment rules, and any resulting transfers can be opened from the request. Requests are under Inventory, Stock Requests, with settings for permissions and virtual locations.

name: stock_request_bom
summary: Lets a stock request be created from a bill of materials, so choosing a product and a quantity fills the request lines with its components. The requested quantity can be adjusted afterwards. It appears as extra fields on the stock request order form.

name: stock_request_direction
summary: Lets users say whether a stock request is to send products out of or bring products into a warehouse, without picking the internal location. Warehouse staff then choose the right route when reviewing the request. The direction is shown on stock requests and request orders.

name: stock_request_kanban
summary: Turns printed kanban cards into stock requests, so when a card's product is used up and the card is scanned, the replenishment is requested automatically. This is a lean way to reorder products that are not stored as normal stock. Cards are created under Inventory, Stock Requests, Stock Requests Kanban, and can be scanned with a barcode reader.

name: stock_request_mrp
summary: Shows the manufacturing orders that were created because a stock request was confirmed, and lets users open them from the request. This ties production back to the request that triggered it. Links appear on the stock request and manufacturing order forms.

name: stock_request_purchase
summary: Shows the purchase orders that were created because a stock request was confirmed, and lets users open them from the request. This ties buying back to the request that triggered it. Links appear on the stock request and purchase order forms.

name: stock_request_submit
summary: Adds a Submitted step to stock requests, so a supervisor can review and correct the route before the request goes ahead. Supervisors see submitted requests and can adjust them. It adds a status and a route field on the stock request.

name: stock_request_tier_validation
summary: Requires stock requests to be approved through tiers before they can be confirmed, such as a warehouse manager then a director. A Request Validation button starts the approvals, and reviews are listed on the request's Reviews tab. Tiers are set under Settings, Technical, Tier Validations.

name: stock_return_request
summary: Lets users return stock from a location to a supplier, a customer, or another internal location by reversing the matching earlier transfers. The user searches for the products and lots to return, and the returns are created from the original pickings. The return request is found under Inventory, Operations, Return Request.

name: account_move_line_stock_info
summary: Shows which stock move each accounting journal line came from, as a column in the journal items list and on the journal item form. Users with access to both Inventory and Accounting can trace an invoice line or journal entry back to its goods movement. The column is hidden by default and can be turned on in the list.

name: procurement_auto_create_group
summary: Creates a new procurement group automatically during each replenishment run, so the transfers from that run contain only that run's moves. Groups are named in a PG sequence and can be seen under Additional info on the transfer. It is enabled per rule in the route settings under Inventory, Configuration, Routes.

name: product_route_profile
summary: Replaces single route settings on products with reusable route profiles, which each contain a set of routes and can be given a priority per company. Profiles are created under Inventory, Configuration, Settings, Routes Profiles and applied from the Inventory tab on the product. It makes it easier to set up the same routes for many products.

name: product_route_profile_internal_resupply
summary: Adds internal supply routes that apply only to chosen products, such as a retail store restocking some items from one warehouse and others from another. These routes are kept out of the shared route profile. It is set on the warehouse and on the product's Inventory tab.

name: stock_archive_constraint
summary: Stops products and storage locations from being archived while they still have stock or related transactions. Users see an error explaining why archiving is blocked. It is part of the warehouse setup and applies to the Products and Locations screens.

name: stock_change_qty_reason
summary: Requires a reason to be recorded when stock quantities are changed by inventory adjustments, either for the whole adjustment or for each line. Admins can also define a list of preset reasons to pick from. Reasons are kept under Inventory, Configuration, Settings, Inventory Adjustment.

name: stock_cycle_count
summary: Plans rolling cycle counts, where small parts of the warehouse are counted on a set schedule instead of doing one full stock take. Each day the system proposes locations to count based on configured rules, and zero-quantity confirmations can be requested to check empty locations. Rules are set under Inventory, Configuration, Cycle Count Rules, and the planned counts appear under Operations.

name: stock_demand_estimate
summary: Lets planners record expected demand for a product at a location over a chosen period, such as expected sales for next month. The estimates are stored as lines for later use, though this module does not use them itself. Lines are created under Inventory, Demand Planning.

name: stock_demand_estimate_matrix
summary: Gives planners a grid view to enter demand estimates for many products across several date periods at once. Periods come from date ranges set under Inventory, Configuration, Date Ranges. Grids are opened from Inventory, Demand Planning, Create Demand Estimates.

name: stock_inventory
summary: Groups inventory adjustments into named inventory counts, so a stock take can be tracked and followed as one document with a clear reference and state. Users pick the products to count by all products, by hand, one product, one lot, or by filter. Groups are listed under Inventory, Operations, Inventory Adjustments.

name: stock_inventory_count_to_zero
summary: Lets users request a count on inventory lines with the count set to zero by default, which is useful for checking that empty locations really are empty. The count is requested from the Inventory Adjustments list with a button. Users then apply the result when ready.

name: stock_inventory_discrepancy
summary: Shows how far each counted line differs from the system quantity and holds an inventory for approval when the difference is above a set threshold. Only users in the Validate All Inventory Adjustments group can approve held counts, while stock users can still validate small differences. Thresholds are set on warehouses and locations.

name: stock_inventory_hide_apply_all
summary: Hides the Apply All button on the inventory adjustments list for everyone, so counts are not applied in one click by accident. Users in the Apply All Inventory Adjustments group can still see the button. It is a simple permission tweak for the Inventory Adjustments screen.

name: stock_inventory_location_state
summary: When an inventory count starts, lists every sub-location under the counted locations and tracks which ones are done. An inventory cannot be validated until all sub-locations have been counted. The progress shows on the inventory form.

name: stock_inventory_lockdown
summary: Blocks stock moves in and out of a location while its inventory count is in progress, and blocks creating or changing locations during the count. Users who try get an error message. It keeps the counted stock steady until the count is finished.

name: stock_inventory_preparation_filter
summary: Adds a Filtered Products option when creating an inventory adjustment, where a domain filter chooses which products to count and update. The filter is shown as a domain widget on the adjustment form. Users start the adjustment from the Inventory Adjustments list.

name: stock_inventory_restriction
summary: Limits who can change or validate inventory adjustments to the users assigned to them, while inventory managers keep full access. It is a permission safeguard for the stock count process. Regular users only see and work on counts they are assigned to.

name: stock_inventory_verification_request
summary: Creates slot verification requests when a count finds a difference above the allowed threshold, so a stock manager can assign someone to recheck that small location. Requests are created from a pending adjustment with a Request Verification button and tracked under Inventory, Inventory Control. The aim is to fix counting errors before the stock moves on.

name: stock_location_bin_name
summary: Builds bin location names automatically from the zone, row, rack, level and box attributes of a location, so names stay consistent. The naming format is set on each location. Warehouse staff see the generated names in location lists and transfers.

name: stock_location_children
summary: Adds a Children button that lists every location below a chosen location at any depth, not only the first level. This makes it easier to see everything stored inside a zone or building. It is found on the location form under Inventory, Configuration, Locations.

name: stock_location_empty
summary: Adds a stock amount to locations and a filter for empty locations, so warehouse staff can quickly find free spaces. The list of locations shows the quantity stored in each one. It is used when looking for places to put new stock.

name: stock_location_fill_state
summary: Labels each location as empty, filled, being filled or being emptied, based on current and planned moves, and lets users filter by that label. It is shown as a column on the Locations list. Customer and supplier locations are excluded to keep the screen fast.

name: stock_location_fill_state_qty_picked
summary: A small link module that makes the fill state of locations account for quantities already picked. It only connects two other modules and has no screens of its own. Users see the more accurate location status in the Locations list.

name: stock_location_is_sublocation
summary: A technical helper that adds a way to check whether a location sits inside another location. It is used by other modules and has no screens of its own. Users see no change.

name: stock_location_lockdown
summary: Lets admins mark internal locations as blocked for storage, so no stock can be put into them. This is useful for parent locations that exist only to group other locations, or for places temporarily taken out of use. The Block Stock Entrance checkbox is set on each location.

name: stock_location_pending_move
summary: Shows the incoming and outgoing moves that are planned for each location, grouped by the location they come from. Users can open them from the location form via Pending Move or Pending Operations. Storage locations need to be enabled first.

name: stock_location_position
summary: Adds position fields to storage locations, such as corridor, row, rack and level, and box coordinates for X, Y and Z. These describe where each location sits physically in the warehouse. Fields appear on the location form under Inventory, Configuration, Locations.

name: stock_location_tray
summary: Organizes a storage location as a grid of cells, such as a tray with rows and columns, and creates the sub-locations for each cell automatically. Tray types define the grid size and are set in Inventory settings, and a location is given a tray type on its form. Moves can then show which cell stock is taken from or put into.

name: stock_location_zone
summary: Classifies storage locations into zones, areas, bins and stock locations so warehouse picking and putaway can be organized by area. A zone is an area that pickers work in, and an area is where stock is put away. Each location shows its kind on its form under Inventory, Configuration, Locations.

name: stock_lot_catalog
summary: A base for showing lots and serial numbers as a catalog of products that users can browse and pick from, similar to the Catalog option in sales and purchases. Lots now carry product attribute values and an image. It is a base that other catalog features build on.

name: stock_lot_catalog_condition
summary: Adds a condition colour to lots in the lot catalog, so a lot's condition such as new or used can be seen at a glance. It builds on the lot catalog and the lot condition feature. Users see the colour in the catalog.

name: stock_lot_catalog_price
summary: Uses the list price of the product as the price of each lot shown in the lot catalog. It connects the lot catalog with the lot list price feature. Users see prices for each lot when browsing.

name: stock_lot_catalog_sale
summary: Adds a Catalog lot option on sales order lines, so a salesperson can browse lots and add them to the order from a catalog window. The lot attribute values are stored on each order line. It is opened from the order lines list of a sales order.

name: stock_lot_catalog_warehouse
summary: Adds a warehouse search panel to the lot catalog, so users can filter the lots shown by warehouse. It connects the lot catalog with the warehouse lot feature. Users pick a warehouse on the side of the catalog view.
